did_you_know.text: The name manna is explained in Exodus through the question “Man hu?”—“What is it?” The English word manna came through Greek and Latin.
A spring forms when groundwater reaches the surface. Springs are especially common where the layers of rock allow water to flow out.
The sages called the seven species listed here “the Seven Species.” In Jewish tradition, the “honey” in this verse is generally understood as date honey.
Ancient copper mines were found in the Timna Valley in the Arava. They show that copper was produced in the region thousands of years ago.
The sages viewed this verse as the source of the commandment to bless after a meal. The familiar wording today consists of several blessings shaped and edited over the centuries.
In the Bible, “heart” often refers to a person’s thoughts, desires, and decisions—not only to the physical organ.
The word chayil does not refer only to physical or military strength. In the Bible, it can also mean wealth, resources, or the ability to accomplish things.
